Tor has never been secure against a “global adversary” — an adversary that can spy on all Tor nodes around the world in real-time — because such an adversary would be able to see traffic from Tor users enter the network, watch it bounce around the world, and then watch it leave the network, making it clear which traffic belongs to which user.

But despite all this, Snowden documents published by The Guardian show that the combined spying power of the Five Eyes (the U.S., U.K., Canada, Australia and New Zealand) doesn’t yet count as a “global adversary,” at least not as of June 2012 when that top-secret presentation was given. It appears that the Western intelligence agencies are only able to opportunistically de-anonymize random unlucky users, and have never been able to de-anonymize a specific user on demand.

I'm not bashful, I'll let you guys know a little bit about me. I live in and or around SLC, Utah. Which means prepper central. Most folks around here own multiple firearms and a good majority have a food / water supply. What does this mean for me?

I have to assume that it's going to be a bloodbath for the first 4-6 weeks. Everybody with a gun is going hunting and it'll get ugly quick. I intend on staying in my basement for the first 2 months. I figure after two months the threat of other people should have passed. They either lived or they didn't but they ain't here kind of thinking.

After that, I'm unsure. Stay or go? Go where? What will be better there? Staying here offers scavenging opportunities, ect.

I own a very decent (my opinion) bob as does my SO. But would we use them? I suppose in the event of a natural (localized) disaster we would. Other than that, it might be safer for me to stay home. But then the question comes up, how long can you live in your house?

I just don't know here. Anybody have any good ideas/thoughts?

It really depends on the nature of the disaster, the timeline of how the disaster develops and the character of the people you're surrounded by. The zombie apocalypse will be different than an EMP, or a Yellowstone eruption, or an economic collapse, or a chemical train derailment. If most of your neighbors are preppers with a strong community fabric then they may self-organize and you'd be better off being out there participating and building ties. Then again, if they get outnumbered by roving hordes of desperate people who know that LDS folks supposedly all stock a year of food in their homes, it might be best to lay low if you have a place to do so that's completely hidden and well fortified.

I plan on staying hunkered down for 6 months. I just made a big post about it in this verse. I don't think it's wise to spend all your money and time investing in world war X.

You bring up a good point of after 2-6 months... what then?

I would try to form groups with my neighbors who made it through the thick of things. We are social creatures. I would try to facilitate the re-opening of my communities clinics, food banks, and things like that.
I wonder how well the communities will stick together? Guess it just depends on the group.

I like the idea of organizing the community quite a bit. The area I live in has quite a bit of land (especially if you count the homes/yards of people who run off or die immediately). If my neighbors and I were able to respond quickly to a disaster, we could probably set up an efficient safe zone, with protection, purified water, and food. How likely do you think it is that a community might be able to stick together instead of turning on each other?
I think the only main factor is resources.

Personally, I don't have a basement, and I'm not sure where I would go if/when things start to calm down. I feel like my neighborhood would be pretty safe for a few days, because a lot of people in the 'burbs have food for a week or more, but after that I just don't know. I would strongly prefer if I was able to just stay put for a while, maybe even indefinitely (I have enough land to grow or raise the food I need). That being said, how do you stay put when you don't have an easily defensible space to wait for the bloodbath to blow over?
